Illustrative design study

A house around a courtyard

An older house re-planned around a small courtyard so light and air reach every room.

Project type
Residential renovation
Setting
Lahore residence
Year
2026
Size
Single-family house

Study facts

  • Scope Renovation of an existing single-family house
  • Key move A small court cut from the centre of the plan
  • Materials Brick, lime plaster and timber

Illustrative design study. Not built work, not a client project.

The brief

The house is a typical older home with deep rooms and dark corridors. The family wants light and air without losing rooms or starting over.

We keep the structure and open a small court at its centre. It becomes the lungs of the house, and every room borrows from it.

The moves

  • A court in the middle. Part of the old roof slab comes out to open the court. No new footprint, no lost plot area.
  • Rooms facing inward. Living, dining and bedrooms open onto the court with full glazing. Corridors shrink as rooms take the view.
  • Shade and breeze first. Deep overhangs, a jali screen and planting keep the court cool through the Lahore summer.
  • One material language. Brick, lime plaster and timber repeat inside and out, so the house reads as one piece.

Takeaways

Light matters more than square footage in a family home.

A courtyard cools the house and cuts daytime lighting bills.

When the structure is sound, renovation beats rebuilding.
Light matters more than square footage in a family home.
